settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: No source line was read showing the saved-connections file being exposed over the network or written with world-readable permissions.
The passphrase constant and cipher are in the database extension; whether the extension is enabled by default was not verified in the read source.
candidates.description: The database extension encrypts persisted saved-connection passwords using a SimpleTextEncryptor built from a constant passphrase. SimpleTextEncryptor selects the weak PBEWithMD5AndDES algorithm, and DatabaseUtils constructs the single static encryptor instance with the literal passphrase "Aa1Gb@tY7_Y". Because the key is hard-coded in the shipped source and the cipher choice is legacy/weak, any party who obtains the saved-connections file (e.g. a copy of the workspace/connections.json) can reproduce the key from the public source and recover the stored database passwords. This is a confidentiality weakness in credential storage. It is reported as a design/cryptography concern limited to the stored-credential data at rest; the source read does not show a remote-triggerable path, only local persistence/read of saved connections.
missing_evidence: Exact line(s) in DatabaseUtils.java writing/reading the saved-connections file and their serialization.
Confirmation of whether the extension is enabled by default and whether the connection store is reachable by other local users.
Review of DatabaseConfiguration/SavedConnectionCommand to confirm passwords are actually encrypted through this encryptor before persistence.
preconditions: The database extension is installed and a user saves a database connection, causing credentials to be persisted.
An attacker obtains a copy of the stored saved-connections file (e.g. connections.json in the workspace).
The attacker has access to the application source/binaries to read the hard-coded passphrase constant.
candidates.title: Database extension uses hard-coded static passphrase to encrypt saved connection credentials
